memory_candidates.content: In this repo, verify-deploy.sh gate 3 / check-extension-docs.sh Rule S checks the DEPLOYED .claude/context/index.json for orphan markdown files, not the source-store index-entries.json directly. Editing only agent-system/extensions/*/index-entries.json (adding an entry or fixing a line_count) will not clear the gate until a redeploy/regenerate step (deploy-headless.sh or the picker's [Regenerate]) propagates the source-store index-entries.json into the deployed .claude/context/index.json. Any task that fixes an index-entries.json mismatch or adds a missing entry must include a redeploy step before re-checking verify-deploy.sh.

errors-append.sh already has an 'update' subcommand (errors-append.sh update --id ERR_ID --fix-status fixed --fixed-date ISO8601 --fix-task N) for closing specs/errors.json ledger entries, but as of this task it has zero callers anywhere in the codebase -- the closure tool exists but nothing (no postflight, no skill) ever invokes it, which is why the ledger only grows. A cheap partial automation would be a plan/task-declared 'resolves_error_ids' field that postflight reads to call errors-append.sh update automatically when the declaring phase's own verification passes; full automatic semantic matching (inferring which entry a change fixes) is not cheap and requires human/agent judgment.

specs/state.json task numbers get renumbered by vault-reset operations (see .claude/rules/state-management.md), which means historical references to task numbers inside specs/errors.json messages and specs/reviews/*.md review reports (e.g. 'spawned task 1007') can go stale/unresolvable against current active_projects without that being a defect -- these files are specs/** artifacts explicitly exempted from the no-task-references rule, and the established precedent (existing reviews/state.json entries citing task numbers like 402/606/817-819 that also don't resolve to current tasks) is to keep the historical number as originally recorded rather than renumber it retroactively.
